summary: I added an analytic search over simplex-shaped sets. These are integer vectors with coordinate sum ≤ n in d dimensions, encoded in base 2n+1, and |A+A| and |A−A| have closed-form counts. The program picks the best (n, d) with at most 4000 points and compares it with the original local search, return

Keep the best simplex-lattice set found by the exact counting formulas, then run a time-bounded local search on it. Each move adds, removes or swaps a point, and the move is kept only if log|A-A| / log|A+A| does not drop; counts are updated incrementally in dictionaries. The simplex is returned if t

Keep the exact-formula simplex as a fallback. Then search weighted simplices {x ≥ 0 : Σ wᵢxᵢ ≤ N} with weights in {1, 2}, scoring each candidate by brute-force numpy counts of A+A and A−A, within a time budget. Return the best set found.

The simplex search was capped by base-(2n+1) encoding, which forces small dimension. I now drop that cap, rank (n,d) by the exact counting formulas, and embed the simplex in the integers with random weights. Exact numpy counts pick the best embedding, and the old exact-base simplex stays as a fallba

I generalize the simplex to a truncated simplex (coordinates in [0,m] with sum ≤ n). Exact numpy DP counts of |A+A| and |A−A| rank all (n, d, m) with at most 4000 points, and the best one is built with base-(2m+1) encoding. The old simplex stays as a fallback.

I generalise the simplex to a slice {x ≥ 0 : a ≤ Σx ≤ b} and rank all (a, b, d) by exact counting formulas for |A+A| and |A−A|. The cap on the integer encoding is relaxed to 1e15, and the chosen set is checked against the old simplex with an exact numpy count before it is returned.

I keep the best exact-formula simplex as the pool and run a time-bounded greedy local search that toggles single points in and out. Pair counts are kept in numpy arrays over the precomputed universe of sums and differences, so each move is evaluated quickly. A move is accepted only if log|A-A|/log|A

I keep the exact-formula simplex as a fallback. The remaining time now goes to simulated annealing over subsets of small boxes {0..m}^d, seeded with a simplex or random points, with fast numpy scoring through linear base encoding. The best set found is returned if it beats the simplex.
